 Oral Judgment

1. The present appeal is filed by the insurance company/original respondent no.3 under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 31.08.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Dahod in MACP No.768 of 2007.

sentences.text: 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that the brother-in-law of the deceased was proceeding towards village Dungali on Motorcycle bearing registration no.GJ 20 C 5173, but NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined near the Village Kachumbar, the said motorcycle break-down and therefore he has informed the deceased, hence, the deceased along with two persons namely Vijaybhai and Kamleshbhai were reached near the spot where the said motorcycle broke-down, and at about 5:30 pm, one truck bearing registration no. GJ 9 Y 6072 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the deceased and other persons, as a result of which the deceased succumbed to the injuries and other persons sustained serious injuries.
Therefore, the claimants have filed petition seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest and costs.

3. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the respondents herein-original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present respondent nos.1 to 6 - original claimants entitled to an amount of Rs.13,16,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.

4. This Court vide order dated 24.07.2014 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant- original insurance company and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned counsel Mr. Hardik Mehta appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined appellant, while assailing the impugned judgment and award, has submitted that that the tribunal erred in concluding that the accident was caused due to sole negligence of driver of the truck and ought to have considered the fact that the deceased was standing on highway and suddenly crossing the road and dashed with the truck.
Therefore, the deceased was himself negligent.

It was further submitted that the income of the deceased considered by the tribunal is on higher side in absence of any documentary evidence produced by the claimants and is required to consider as per the minimum wages schedule.
That, the tribunal has erred in applying the multiplier of 15 and considering the age of the deceased at the time of accident, the multiplier should be applied.
That, the tribunal erred in awarding the amount under the conventional heads and is required to be reduced.

6. By making the aforesaid submissions on the quantum and negligency, learned Advocate for the appellant prayed this Court to consider the contributory negligency of the deceased as well and also to reduce the amount of compensation granted by the learned Tribunal.

7. Per contra, Learned advocate Mr. Hiren Modi appearing for the respondent nos. 1 to 7- original claimants submit that the findings of the tribunal is just and proper in determining the negligency issue and also in determining the income.

It is contended by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined the learned advocate that the tribunal has failed to consider future rise of income for the computation of future loss.

That, the deceased was 44 years old and in view of the National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi,
reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 25% addition towards future prospect should have been considered by the tribunal.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the respondents - original claimants would further submit that this is a case where the compensation awarded by the tribunal is required to be enhanced by recalculating under the principle of just and fair compensation.

He would further submit that though the claimants have not filed the cross objection or cross appeal for enhancement of the claim amount, looking to the computation of the income and other heads of granting compensation, this Court ought to have arrived at just, fair and equitable compensation and award the same and prayed to dismiss the appeal, however, requested this Court to enhance the compensation.

9. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined and perused impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation and negligency.

So far as issue of negligency is concerned, the tribunal held that there was ample space on the road to pass any vehicle, even the truck stopped after 20 feet from the place of accident, therefore, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the truck driver.
Looking to the evidence on record including the FIR and place of panchnama, there is no dispute that there is a curve near the bridge.
In such type of roads, any prudent person may have avoided the risk and driven the truck in slow speed with reasonable care.
Even after the accident, he failed to stop the truck.
Under such circumstances, the findings of the tribunal with regard to the issue of negligency is just and proper and the contention regarding contributory negligency stands rejected.

10. As regards the findings of the tribunal on assessing the income of the deceased is concerned, it was submitted that in the claim petition that the deceased was doing carpentry work and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
The claimants have produced copy of bills vide exh. 34 to 42, in which, one of the bill was from year 1994.
The tribunal has rightly considered that the deceased was working as a skilled carpenter since year 1994 at least.

Considering the nature of work in which the deceased was involved, evidence on record and the experience of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined the deceased in his skill-work, the tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- per month at the time of accident.
11. Sofar as future prospect is concerned, the tribunal has not given any future rise of income.

However, considering the ratio laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 25% addition towards future prospect is given for the age group of 40 to 50 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the deceased was aged about 44 years.
For this age group, 25% additional compensation is prescribed in the Pranav Shetty case.

Accordingly, the income of the deceased would come to Rs.9000*25%
(2250) =11,250/-.
12.

Considering the fact that the deceased was survived by widow, one minor daughter and two major sons mother and father, as per the ration laid down in the decision of Supreme Court in the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Sitaben Wd-O Naranbhai Ramabhai ... on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96771393/
3 case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, 1/4th deduction has been applied towards spend by the deceased on himself.

sentences.text: After 1/4th deduction towards personal expense of the deceased, the calculation of the income the deceased is Rs.8440/-(Rs.11250/- - Rs.2810/- (1/4th deduction towards personal expenses).

13. Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 44 years NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. (supra) and the scheduled prescribed, the Tribunal has erred in applying the multiplier.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the calculation of the future loss, multiplier of 14 would be applied.

Thus, the future loss benefit is determined as Rs.8440/-*12*14 (Multiplier) which comes to Rs.14,17,920/-.
14.
This brings me to the issue of loss of consortium.
In the present case, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- under the head of the loss of consortium.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram &
Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium to the tune of Rs.1,93,600/- (Rs.48,400/- X 4),
as two of the children of the deceased was major at the time of the accident, they would not be able to claim the compensation under this head.

sentences.text: Lastly, the amount to be awarded under the conventional heads, more particularly, funeral expenses and the loss of estate is also required to be reconsidered in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
The same is to be considered as Rs.18,150/- respectively.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined 15.

Another issue arises as to whether in absence of any cross objection or cross appeal on behalf of the claimant, whether in the appeal filed by the insurance company the appellate Court can enhance the compensation granted by the tribunal.

O.41 R.33 of CPC r/w O.41 R.22 read with decision in case of Surekha W/o Rajendra Nakhate Versus Santosh S/o Namdeo Jadhav [2021 (16) SCC 467]
would rescue the situation.

entities.text: Surekha W/o Rajendra Nakhate Versus Santosh S/o Namdeo Jadhav [2021 (16) SCC 467]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Needless to say that principle of just and fair compensation applies at every stage of proceedings.
The duty is casted upon the Court to assess, calculate and grant just and fair compensation at every stage regardless of filing of appeal.
Therefore, it is clear that even in absence of cross-objection or cross appeal the appellate Court holds jurisdiction to enhance the just compensation.

16. Therefore, original claimants - respondents herein are entitled to enhanced amount as computed hereunder:

 (monthly)

Deduction of amount (after deduction: Rs.8,440) spent by the deceased on himself Future Loss 8440*12*14 = Rs.14,17,920/-

The original claimants are held entitled to compensation of an amount of Rs.16,47,820/-.

Since by impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.13,16,000/-, the claimants shall be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.3,31,820/- (Rs.16,47,820- Rs.13,16,000/-)
with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization.
The original opponents are held jointly and severally liable to pay such enhanced amount of compensation with proportionate costs and interest.
Rest of the direction(s) of the tribunal remains same.
18. Let, the aforesaid amount be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the present order.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to release and disburse the entire award amount in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:

19. Let, such exercise be undertaken by the Tribunal strictly in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard; preferably within a period of two weeks from deposit of such amount.
